title: Unique differential on one filtered-complex quotient page
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], $K^\bullet$ an integer-indexed cochain complex, and $F$ a decreasing filtration by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Fix $r\in\mathbb Z$ with $r\ge1$. Write $Z_r^{p,q}=F.\mathrm{complexCycles}(p,p+q,r)$ and $B_r^{p,q}=F.\mathrm{complexBoundaries}(p,p+q,r)$ [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients], and form the actual object $Q_r^{p,q}=\operatorname{coker}(B_r^{p,q}\hookrightarrow Z_r^{p,q})$ using [lem-sp-filtered-complex-boundaries-le-cycles]. There is a unique family of morphisms between these quotient objects, zero outside bidegree $(r,1-r)$ [def-sp-spectral-sequence], with square zero and the following representative equation. For any object A, related bidegrees i,j, maps t:A->F^(i.1)K^(i.1+i.2) and tprime:A->F^(j.1)K^(j.1+j.2), and maps x:A->Z_r^i and y:A->Z_r^j, if dt=tprime in K and x,y project respectively to the graded classes of t,tprime, then x followed by the quotient projection and the differential equals y followed by the target quotient projection. This is exactly the data type FilteredComplexPageDifferential; no successor homology is asserted.

source.place: Tag 012K, displayed cycle, boundary and differential formulas and lemma-spectral-sequence-filtered-complex

proof.text: The unchanged page objects and projections are the actual cokernels of the proved boundary inclusions. For every related pair obtain a descended map with its full representative equation from the single-map descent lemma. Define d on related pairs by that map and zero elsewhere; its representative equation follows by reducing the dependent if.

For two related consecutive pairs obtain A,t,tprime,x,y with x epic from the proved representative-cover lemma. The composite x π_i is epic. Precomposing d(i,j)d(j,k) gives y π_j d(j,k). Differentiating tprime is zero, by its equality with dt and K.d_comp_d. Apply the representative equation to tprime and the zero representative at k: y π_j d(j,k)=0. Cancel x π_i. If either pair is unrelated, one factor is zero by construction. This proves square-zero and shape and hence constructs the data record.

For any other data record E, compare each component with the constructed D. At a related pair use the same representative cover and precompose with epic x π_i. Both maps give y π_j by their representative equations, so epi cancellation gives equality. At a nonrelated pair both components are zero. Function extensionality identifies their d fields and proof irrelevance identifies the remaining structure fields. This gives existence and uniqueness without any new homology claim.
